impact.user_visible: Prediction requests returned 500 for roughly a fifth of traffic; dispatch clients saw 'estimate unavailable' and two support tickets were raised.

root_cause: Release v5 expects a traffic_index feature that the request schema does not provide. The model artifact and the service contract disagreed, so every request that reached the model raised KeyError: 'traffic_index' and returned 500.
contributing_factors: The release gate was overridden for a hotfix, so the schema contract test never ran against v5.
The rollout went to 100% of traffic with no canary, so the mismatch reached all requests immediately.
Detection was fast but response was not: paging at 02:12, acknowledgement at 02:22, rollback at 04:20 because the rollback path required a release approval that had no out-of-hours route.
detection: http_5xx_rate_high fired at 02:18 (first error at 02:00:04, present in the log but not alerted on). The latency alert at 02:12 was the first page. On-call acknowledged 11 minutes after the page.

immediate_action.verified_by: 5xx rate returned to 0.001 and p95 latency to 190ms within four minutes of the alias change; alert resolved at 04:24.

timeline.event: v5 starts and logs a feature-schema mismatch warning
feature mismatch hypothesised from the startup warning

prevention: Run the service contract test against the artifact inside the release gate, and block promotion when the request schema and model signature disagree.
Require a canary stage at 5% of traffic for 30 minutes with automatic rollback on 5xx rate, so a schema mismatch affects a bounded audience.
Give the on-call engineer a pre-approved rollback that needs no release approval outside working hours; rehearse it monthly and time it.
Page on the 5xx rate directly rather than on latency, and alert when the service logs a startup schema warning.
